page.title: Style
page.purpose: Inspect, edit, and fork one style. This is where the taxonomy is authored, so it must teach the vocabulary through use rather than assume it.

priorities.statement: Editing an axis re-renders the specimen immediately.
priorities.notes: The connection between a parameter and its visual consequence is the thing being taught. A form that requires a save to see the effect breaks that loop.

priorities.statement: The strategy governs which fields are shown.
priorities.notes: A procedural style shows no generation block; a guided style shows the scaffold. Displaying inapplicable fields would invite the contradictions the catalog refuses at write.

priorities.statement: Reserved regions are drawn on the specimen, not typed as four numbers.
priorities.notes: It is a spatial decision and should be made spatially, with the numeric values shown alongside for precision.

priorities.statement: Forking is offered wherever an edit is refused.
priorities.notes: A style referenced by a released backdrop is immutable. The refusal should present forking as the path forward rather than as a dead end.

states.description: The style with a live specimen, its axes, treatment chain, reserved-region overlay, and gate thresholds.
Fields are live; the specimen re-renders as parameters change. Unsaved changes are indicated.
The version is referenced by a released backdrop and cannot be edited. Names the referencing release and offers to fork into a new version.
A write was refused. Names the offending axis, value, or strategy contradiction — for example a guided style with no scaffold.
A new style derived from this one, showing its parent reference and which axes were changed.
The style does not exist. Offers the catalog and any close identifier match.
